titre: The Face That Restoration Gave Back to the Mystic Lamb
accroche: For nearly five centuries, the most-looked-at face on the Ghent Altarpiece was not the one the Van Eyck brothers had painted.
contenu_vulgarise:
Since 1432, millions of visitors have stopped in front of the Mystic Lamb, the central panel of the Ghent Altarpiece painted by the Van Eyck brothers, where a lamb stands on an altar. In 2019, a team of restorers from the Royal Institute for Cultural Heritage in Brussels removes a thin layer of paint that had covered this face for nearly five centuries. The face that appears is not the one the world knew.

## The Mechanism

The team does not discover this difference at the moment of stripping. Before touching the panel, it maps the chemical composition of the surface by X-ray fluorescence and infrared imaging, two techniques that pass through layers of paint without damaging them. Beneath the visible layer, these maps reveal two superimposed sets of eyes and two pairs of nostrils: one version, the closest to the surface, matches the familiar lamb, with its gaze turned outward; another, older and slightly offset, suggests a shorter muzzle and eyes turned toward the viewer. Everything indicates that a 16th-century overpaint replaced the original face with a more neutral version, while enlarging the head along the neck.

When the overpaint is actually removed, the face brought to light matches what the imaging had predicted: piercing, close-set eyes, a short muzzle, an expression that several commentators call disconcerting. A study published in 2020 in the journal Science Advances confirms, by the same methods applied this time to the entire panel, that this restoration does correspond to the intention of the two painter brothers.

## What This Shifts

The altarpiece thus changed not once but twice: in 1432, then around 1550, with no written record to warn later generations of the substitution. For nearly five hundred years, a replacement face stood in for the original in everyone's eyes, restorers included, until an imaging technique invisible to the naked eye flushed it out from under the layer that covered it.

The public's reaction to the discovery, somewhere between unease and mockery on social media, shows how far the replaced image had itself become, in the minds of those who had looked at it for generations, the authentic work: people had not grown used to a fake by mistake, they had become attached to it. Restoring an original therefore does not only give back a material truth; it also takes away from generations of visitors the image they had come to hold as the true one.

repere.texte: The Ghent Altarpiece is completed in 1432 by the Van Eyck brothers. An overpaint applied around 1550 masks the Lamb's original face for nearly five centuries, until its removal in 2019 and its scientific confirmation in 2020.
repere.source: Van der Snickt et al., Science Advances, 2020

carte.punch: The face of the Mystic Lamb known for centuries was not the one painted in 1432.
carte.idee: In 2019, restorers remove a 16th-century overpaint that covered the face of Van Eyck's Mystic Lamb. The original face, with eyes turned toward the viewer, had been replaced without any written record of it for almost five hundred years.

quiz.question: How did the restorers know, even before removing the overpaint, that the Lamb's original face differed from the one known for centuries?
choix: A separate preparatory drawing by Van Eyck already showed a face different from the familiar one
An X-ray examination detected an old hole in the panel at the location of the face
Chemical imaging revealed, beneath the visible layer, a second, smaller set of eyes and nostrils
A 16th-century written document precisely described the change of face
quiz.explication: X-ray fluorescence and infrared imaging detected beneath the overpaint two pairs of nostrils and two superimposed sets of eyes, one Eyckian, the other later, before the overpaint was physically removed.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Which technique made it possible to detect the two superimposed pairs of nostrils beneath the overpaint, even before it was removed?
quiz_supplementaire.explication: X-ray fluorescence maps the chemical composition of the surface without damaging it, and revealed two superimposed pairs of nostrils beneath the overpaint.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What else did the 16th-century overpaint change, besides the Lamb's face?
choix: It added a halo that did not exist in the original version
It enlarged the head along the neck
It replaced the altar with a landscape
It changed the color of the lamb's fleece
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text specifies that the 16th-century overpaint also enlarged the lamb's head along the neck, at the same time as it replaced the face.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What was the public's reaction to the discovery of the new face in 2019?
choix: Near-total indifference, the subject interesting only specialists
An official request to restore the old overpaint, judged more faithful
Unease and mockery, notably on social media
A scientific controversy over the reliability of infrared imaging
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text describes a reaction ranging from unease to mockery on social media, showing the public's attachment to the replaced face.
